key_insight: Motile microorganisms can self-organize into bioconvective flows that passively enhance heat transfer, offering a bio-inspired route to lower-energy thermal management.
engineering_relevance: Bioconvection could help reduce pumping power, weaken thermal boundary layers, and improve cooling performance in hybrid systems for data centers and other high-heat technologies.
method: Reviewed natural and laboratory studies of microorganism-induced flow and pattern formation.
Synthesized thermofluidic transport mechanisms and relevant non-dimensional numbers.
Assessed thermal performance to judge feasibility for practical cooling applications.
evidence_signal: The paper supports its claims with quantitative analyses of bioconvective thermal performance and interpretation through dimensionless flow and heat-transfer metrics.
watch_item: Practical deployment is constrained by microbial stability, material compatibility, controllability, scalability, and integration with existing cooling hardware.
paper_title: Engineering Collective Microbial Dynamics for Sustainable Thermal Management
